faq.title: What biomedical engineers ask us
faq.q1: How long does spare part delivery take?
faq.a1: We reply to your request within 72 business hours and deliver the spare part in 72 hours. Importing the original part usually takes 8 to 12 weeks.
faq.q2: Do I need to send the broken part?
faq.a2: Ideally, yes: we scan the physical part to rebuild it and correct wear. If you don't have it, we can start from technical drawings.
faq.a3: No. We work with PETG and ABS, which withstand chemical disinfectants and hospital cold disinfection, but are not suitable for autoclaving.
faq.a4: Technical-grade polymers such as PETG and ABS, and resins for parts that need finer detail.

rubric.title: Hybrid Assessment & Certification System
rubric.subtitle: To obtain the official Novaforte certification at any level, we evaluate both digital mastery in software and the physical functionality of the manufactured object.
rubric.digitalDesc: Evaluation of software design: fully constrained sketches, efficient use of parametric operations, clean three-dimensional meshes, and optimized slicing settings.
rubric.physicalDesc: Evaluation of the printed part: verification of physical tolerances and clearances (functional assemblies), mechanical resistance of layers/infill under impact or tensile stress, and final surface quality.
rubric.badgeDesc: The student must achieve a minimum score of 80% in both components (digital and physical) to receive their official Novaforte Maker skills certificate.

curriculum.title: Detailed Study Plan
curriculum.subtitle: Click on each level to learn about the technical focus, software tools, and suggested practical projects.

level1.title: Level 1: Introduction to Spatial Thinking and Intuitive CAD Modeling (10 Hours)
level1.software: Tinkercad / Tinkercad Classrooms and introduction to Orca Slicer / Creality Print
level1.project: Design a 'Personalized Pocket Object' (e.g. modular key organizer, ergonomic tag, or a mini functional utility accessory) with geometric addition and subtraction.
level1.learn1: Class 1: The Jump into Three Dimensions. Fundamentals of Additive Manufacturing. Cartesian operation of 3D printers (X, Y, Z axes), PLA filament properties. Practice: Tinkercad profile configuration and basic primitive shapes.
level1.learn2: Class 2: Addition, Subtraction, and Creative Modification. Geometric algebra and boolean operations. Solids vs holes and alignment. Practice: guided design of a mug with handle and millimetric hollows.
level1.learn3: Class 3: Material Limits and Custom Design. Design rules for additive manufacturing (DFAM), bridges and critical angles > 45°. Practice: sketching and digital modeling of the pocket object.
level1.learn4: Class 4: Slicing Basic and Technical Closure (File Freeze). Introduction to Orca Slicer / Creality Print. Layer height, infill, and STL export. Control: dimensions technical validation and platform upload.
level1.learn5: Class 5: Physical Phase, Post-Processing, and Certification. Physical materialization. Safe post-processing: removal of strings/supports. Graduation: showcase, aesthetic evaluation, and certificate delivery.

level2.title: Level 2: Parametric Design and Functional Mechanical Assemblies (15 Hours)
level2.software: Onshape (Cloud industrial CAD) or Autodesk Fusion 360
level2.project: Design a 'Rubber Band-Powered Impeller Car' (modeling chasis, functional wheels, transmission shafts, and brackets with precise clearances).
level2.learn1: Class 1: From 2D Sketch to Parametric Solid. Parametric design fundamentals, technical drawing and views (front, top, side). Sketching and extruding. Practice: Onshape and sketches with dimensions and constraints.
level2.learn2: Class 2: Geometric Constraints and Design Intent. Sketch relations (coincidence, tangency, symmetry) and design intent. Practice: model a support plate with slots and change the master length dimension.
level2.learn3: Class 3: Simple Mechanics, Fits, and Real Tolerances. Thermal contraction of polymers. Functional clearances (0.2 to 0.4 mm) and press-fits. Practice: wheels and axles modeling for the Impeller Car.
level2.learn4: Class 4: Assembly Verification and Advanced Slicing (File Freeze). Advanced slicing, tree supports, and perimeters. Assemblies and collision detection in Onshape. Control: virtual assembly test and file freeze.
level2.learn5: Class 5: Factory Assembly Line and Performance Testing. Industrial assembly and fitting. Failure analysis on physical tolerances. Graduation: guided assembly, track tests, and diplomas.

level3.title: Level 3: Product Engineering and Collective Co-Creation Lab (15 Hours)
level3.project: Design a 'Co-Creation Route' (Technical: interactive STEAM educational kit for school labs; Artistic: custom author sculpture with complex volume).
level3.tech1: Class 1: Project Methodology (Agile/Scrum) & Roles. Engineering group roles assignment. Challenge technical requirements audit and Onshape workspace configuration.
level3.tech2: Class 2: Cloud Collaborative Concurrent Modeling. Multibody modeling strategies in Onshape and design based on shared global variables. Real-time digital version merging practice.
level3.tech3: Class 3: Structural Optimization. Empirical mechanical stress analysis and weight optimization using ribs. Technical Peer-Review session.
level3.tech4: Class 4: Technical Certification and G-Code (File Freeze). G-code deep analysis, critical perimeter manual configuration, and thermal control. Final assembly validation.
level3.tech5: Class 5: Systems Integration & Graduation. Complex sociomaterial systems integration (STEAM). Final assembly and dynamic system integration. 5-minute pitch.
level3.art1: Class 1: Polygonal Modeling Fundamentals. Introduction to Blender interface, keyboard shortcuts, 3D navigation, and geometry manipulation. 'Sandbox' modeling exercise.
level3.art2: Class 2: Transition to Digital Sculpting. Dynamic brush usage (Draw, Clay, Smooth, Grab) and symmetry. Silhouette blockout and proportions definition.
level3.art3: Class 3: Topology and Print Preparation. Extreme overhang analysis on organic meshes, decimation, and remesh in Blender. Thicken fragile limbs for bed adhesion.
level3.art4: Class 4: Organic Supports and G-Code (File Freeze). Tree supports configuration and mastery to protect fine textures without marking visible surfaces.
level3.art5: Class 5: Aesthetic Finish & Graduation. Meticulous organic supports removal and aesthetic finish techniques for piece exhibition. Close: Art show presentation.

rows.col4: Basic sketching, boolean logic, structural slicing parameters, and physical post-processing.
2D technical drawing, dimensions, constraints, tolerances, and gears.
Agile/Scrum hardware methodology, cloud collaborative concurrent design, DfAM optimization, digital sculpting, and pitch.
